metaTitle: AHC30722 Cert III in Horticulture RPL — Gardener
metaDescription: Experienced gardener? Get the AHC30722 Certificate III in Horticulture through RPL using your work experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The AHC30722 Certificate III in Horticulture is the trade qualification for gardeners and horticulturists. If you already maintain gardens, parks or nurseries, RPL recognises your experience so you get the qualification without a full apprenticeship.
whoIsItFor:
• Gardeners in councils, schools, resorts and private estates
  • Parks and grounds staff
  • Nursery and production horticulture workers
  • Gardening business owners

You'll usually have two or more years of hands-on horticulture work: identifying and selecting plants, pruning, controlling weeds, pests and diseases, improving soil, running irrigation and using machinery and chemicals safely.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of your work: planting, pruning, maintenance, irrigation
  • Maintenance schedules, plant lists and job sheets
  • Chemical application records and chemical licences or accreditation
  • Machinery tickets, such as chainsaw or ride-on mower training
  • A reference from your employer or clients
licensingInfo: Applying chemicals commercially may need a chemical user licence or accreditation in your state, and some work, such as tree work near power lines, has its own rules. The qualification doesn't replace those licences.
description:
The AHC30722 Certificate III in Horticulture covers the skills of a qualified gardener: identifying and selecting plants, specialist amenity pruning, controlling weeds, pests and diseases, improving soil, operating pressurised irrigation, operating machinery, transporting, storing and applying chemicals, WHS and sustainable work practices.

Electives cover areas such as arboriculture, parks and gardens, turf and nursery work. It replaces AHC30716.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate III in Horticulture through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have broad horticulture experience. Photos, maintenance records, chemical records and a reference are assessed against the units, with practical skills observed or recorded.

faqs.q: Does it include a chemical licence?
faqs.a: No. Chemical user licences or accreditation are separate. If you already hold one, it's useful evidence for the chemical units.

faqs.q: Can my overseas gardening experience count?
faqs.a: Yes. Overseas experience can be assessed, especially with a reference and recent Australian work.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than an apprenticeship. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: AHC30921 Landscape Construction RPL — Cert III
metaDescription: Experienced landscaper? Get the AHC30921 Certificate III in Landscape Construction through RPL. The usual licence qualification in QLD and NSW.
heroIntro: The AHC30921 Certificate III in Landscape Construction is the trade qualification for landscapers. If you already build paving, retaining walls, drainage and garden structures, RPL recognises your experience so you get the qualification without a full apprenticeship.
whoIsItFor:
• Landscapers and landscape construction workers
  • Paving, retaining wall and hardscape specialists
  • Landscaping business owners
  • Landscapers who trained overseas

You'll usually have two or more years of broad landscape construction: setting out sites, drainage, paving, retaining walls, brick, block, stone and concrete features, and planting.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of completed jobs, from set-out to finish
  • Plans, quotes and job sheets you've worked from
  • A reference from your employer, builder or clients
  • Tickets such as the White Card and plant operation
  • Any licences you already hold
licensingInfo:
Structural landscaping work above a set value needs a contractor licence in some states. In Queensland, the QBCC issues structural landscaping licences, and in NSW, Fair Trading licenses structural landscaping. This qualification is the usual trade qualification for those licences, along with experience and other requirements.

Rules differ between states. We can explain your state's steps when you apply.
description:
The AHC30921 Certificate III in Landscape Construction is the national trade qualification for landscapers. It covers setting out sites, installing drainage, implementing paving and retaining wall projects, constructing brick, block, stone and concrete features and stone cladding, giving information on plants, plant establishment and soil improvement.

It replaces AHC30916.

faqs.q: Can I get a landscaping qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have broad landscape construction experience. Photos of your jobs, plans and a reference are assessed against the units, with practical skills observed or recorded.

faqs.q: Do I need this qualification for a landscaping licence?
faqs.a: In states that license structural landscaping, such as Queensland and NSW, it is the usual trade qualification for the licence. Each regulator also asks for experience and other requirements.

faqs.q: I mainly do paving and retaining walls. Is that enough?
faqs.a: It's a good start, but the qualification also covers drainage, features and planting. If you have gaps, gap training can cover them.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than an apprenticeship. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: AHC40422 Cert IV in Horticulture RPL — Supervisor
metaDescription: Horticulture supervisor or specialist? Get the AHC40422 Certificate IV in Horticulture through RPL using your experience. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The AHC40422 Certificate IV in Horticulture is the qualification for horticulture supervisors and specialists. If you already plan planting programs, manage soil health and lead teams, RPL turns that experience into a nationally recognised qualification.
whoIsItFor:
• Horticulture supervisors and team leaders
  • Parks and gardens coordinators
  • Nursery managers and production supervisors
  • Horticultural consultants and business owners

You'll usually have several years in horticulture, including planning planting programs, managing soil health and plant nutrition, supervising staff and running WHS and sustainability practices.
evidenceExamples:
• Planting programs and landscape maintenance plans you've written
  • Soil tests and nutrition programs you've developed
  • Rosters, work plans and supervision records
  • WHS and environmental procedures you manage
  • A reference from your manager or clients
description:
The AHC40422 Certificate IV in Horticulture covers supervisory and specialist horticulture: developing soil health and plant nutrition programs, planning plant establishment, maintaining WHS processes, and implementing and monitoring sustainable work practices.

Electives cover areas such as parks and gardens, nursery production, arboriculture, turf and team leadership. It replaces AHC40416 and AHC40410.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate IV in Horticulture through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you supervise or plan horticulture work. Your planting programs, soil and nutrition plans, supervision records and a reference are assessed against the units.

faqs.q: Do I need the Certificate III first?
faqs.a: No, there are no entry requirements. Experienced horticulturists can go straight to the Certificate IV.
Mostly. Evidence is submitted online, and your workplace confirms your skills.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.
